Hi Marissa,

First drafts are ready for your review! I've attached the Standard and Signature editions of both the resume and cover letter, so four documents total.

Quick orientation on what you're looking at:

The **Standard editions** are your ATS-optimized Word and PDF versions, built to pass through automated screening systems for online applications. Clean, professional, easy for you to update yourself down the road.

The **Signature editions** are the designed Canva versions, branded to you and built to stand out when you're sending directly to a hiring manager, networking, or following up after a conversation. Same content, different presentation.

A few things to know as you read through:

Since your questionnaire had some open spots, I filled in a few gaps with educated guesses based on your old resume. The big ones are your timeline (Redwood Pathways as 2013 to 2020, your freelance executive support services as 2016 to 2024, and Cedarstone Collective from September 2023 forward), and the positioning, which I aimed at Administrative Operations/Office Manager roles since that's where your experience is strongest. I also cut Harbor & Finch since it's older than 12 years and didn't add to the story.

I've attached a short follow-up document with a handful of quick questions, mostly to confirm dates and pull out a few specific wins from your Cedarstone Collective role. Even a few words on each will let me sharpen the next draft considerably.

Take your time reading through everything. When you're ready, send back any edits, reactions, or answers to those questions and I'll fold them in. The first of the four included revision rounds starts here, so don't hold back; this is the time to tell me what feels right and what doesn't.

Looking forward to your thoughts!

Darius

source_message.text:
Hi Marissa,

I'm so sorry, I had reviewed the answers but then at some point had it in my mind I was waiting for a response from you—my mistake! They were really helpful, and I've now updated both the resume and cover letter to reflect everything you shared. New versions are attached.

A few things to know about what changed:

The biggest shift is the overall positioning. Based on what you said about being open to something new and not necessarily targeting assistant roles, I rebuilt the resume around remote operations instead. The headline, summary, and core competencies now lead with operations, logistics, customer relations, and process building, which opens you up to a much wider set of remote roles (operations coordinator, customer operations, logistics coordinator, project coordinator, that kind of range) without losing the personal assistant experience, which is still in your work history. The cover letter follows the same direction and explicitly names the kinds of roles you are open to, so a hiring manager is not left guessing.

I also corrected the timeline: Redwood Pathways now shows 2013 to 2017, and your freelance executive support services shows 2014 to Present with a small "(Concurrent)" note so the overlap with Cedarstone Collective reads as intentional rather than confusing. Let me know if you would rather drop that label; it is completely optional.

Your Lakeview Design College qualification is now accurately shown (Associate of Science in Retail Management), and I leaned into your "built everything from the ground up" answer for Cedarstone Collective. That actually became one of the strongest parts of the resume; your builder mindset comes through really clearly.

If anything reads off—dates that need adjusting, language that does not sound like you, or anything missing—just let me know and I will fold it in.

Take your time; there is no rush.

Thank you,
Darius
